problem.name: Binary integer programming
problem.statement_latex:
Given $A\in\mathbb Z^{d\times n}$ and $b\in\mathbb Z^d$, find $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ satisfying $Ax\leq b$, or decide infeasibility. An additional profit threshold converts a linear optimization problem into this form. The regime of interest has fixed or slowly growing $d$ and binary-encoded coefficients.
The few-inequality quantum bound uses coherent-memory time with bit-arithmetic costs, classical meet in the middle uses RAM time, and bounded-row-arity encodings use bit complexity.
problem.statement_text: Given $A\in\mathbb Z^{d\times n}$ and $b\in\mathbb Z^d$, find $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ satisfying $Ax\leq b$, or decide infeasibility. An additional profit threshold converts a linear optimization problem into this form. The regime of interest has fixed or slowly growing $d$ and binary-encoded coefficients. The few-inequality quantum bound uses coherent-memory time with bit-arithmetic costs, classical meet in the middle uses RAM time, and bounded-row-arity encodings use bit complexity.

quantum.details_latex: The polynomial arithmetic factors depend on coefficient bit length. For $d=o(n/\log n)$, the time is $2^{(1/3+o(1))n}$. Precomputed partial-sum vectors support coherent multidimensional range queries; both preprocessing and searching are included in the bound. With $B$-bit coefficients, direct arithmetic and comparisons have reversible cost polynomial in $dn(B+\log n)$.

classical.headline_latex: $O^*(2^{n/2})$ for fixed $d$, meet in the middle with dominance searching.
classical.headline_text: $O^*(2^{n/2})$ for fixed $d$, meet in the middle with dominance searching.
classical.details_latex: The two lists of partial-sum vectors are combined by coordinatewise inequalities and use exponential memory. For a different regime in which every row has support at most a fixed $r$, encode each forbidden local assignment as a clause using the original $n$ Boolean variables. Polynomially many rows then give $\operatorname{poly}(\text{input size})2^{O_r(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ deterministic time and polynomial space; linearly many rows improve the exponent to $O_r(n/\sqrt{\log n})$. A fixed number of dense, large-coefficient inequalities retains the few-constraint meet-in-the-middle comparison.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant for fixed $d$ and unrestricted row support, using Grover search and amplitude amplification. Bounded-row-arity instances have the stronger subexponential classical comparator.

evidence.description_latex: Rigorous quantum upper bounds in the specified access model, with partial evidence against the best displayed classical algorithms in the few-dense-inequality regime.

hardware.description_latex: The active assignment register has $n$ qubits; $d$ arithmetic accumulators require input-dependent bit width. Exponential coherent range-search data and long searches dominate large-instance implementation. Increasing $d$ raises both the $n^d$ factor and arithmetic cost.
